title: Duality of majority Fourier coefficients
statement: Let $m\in\mathbb N$ and let $S,T\subseteq[2m+1]$ satisfy $|S|+|T|=2m+2$. For the majority function on $\{0,1\}^{2m+1}$, whose value is $1$ when more than $m$ coordinates are false and $-1$ otherwise, the Fourier--Walsh coefficients satisfy $\widehat M_m(S)=(-1)^m\widehat M_m(T)$.
replaced:
Let $m\in\mathbb N$, put $n=2m+1$, and define $M_m:\{\pm1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ by
$M_m(x)=1$ when more than $m$ coordinates equal $1$, and $M_m(x)=-1$ otherwise.
For $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ define
$\widehat M_m(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{\pm1\}^n}M_m(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i$.
If $S,T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ satisfy $|S|+|T|=2m+2$, then
\[
 \widehat M_m(S)=(-1)^m\widehat M_m(T).
\]
